summary:
PROJECT NAME: THE SILENCE WE LEFT
Project Title: After the Last Signal

1. Project Description
After the Last Signal is an interactive 3D space exploration and educational website developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It showcases spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space after their missions.
2. Why Did We Develop This Project?
We developed this project to bring attention to forgotten space artifacts whose stories are often overlooked. We believe space exploration does not end when a mission is completed. Our aim is to preserve these stories and inspire future generations.
3. Problem Statement
Many people know about successful space missions but are unaware of what happens to spacecraft and equipment after their missions end. Their historical and scientific importance is often overlooked.
4. Our Solution
Our website makes space history engaging through interactive exploration and storytelling. Users can:
- Explore a virtual 3D space environment.
- Discover 13 space artifacts.
- Learn about historical missions and milestones.
- Access NASA images and official resources.
- Participate in quizzes.
- Leave messages for future explorers through a Time Capsule.
5. Objective:Our goal is to preserve the stories of forgotten space artifacts, increase awareness of humanity's achievements in space exploration, and make space education accessible and engaging.

Our Message: Even after the last signal, the story continues.
details: 1. What exactly does it do? After the Last Signal is an interactive educational web experience created around the idea of exploring what happens to space missions and spacecraft after their final communication or when their active missions come to an end. The project presents NASA space missions and abandoned or inactive space hardware through an engaging, story-driven digital experience. Instead of presenting the information only as static facts, it allows users to explore mission information, understand the final stages of spacecraft operations, and learn about the scientific and historical importance of equipment that remains in space or on other celestial bodies. The project focuses on turning complex space-science information into something that is easier and more interesting for students and the general public to understand. It combines storytelling, visual presentation, interactive elements, and NASA-related information to create a more immersive learning experience. The central idea is that the end of communication does not mean the end of a mission's story. Even after a spacecraft becomes silent or a mission is completed, the hardware, data, discoveries, and lessons from that mission continue to have scientific and historical value. 2. How does it work? The project works as a browser-based interactive website. Users can navigate through the different sections of the experience and explore information related to space missions and their final stages. The website presents information in a visually engaging way so that users can understand the journey from an active mission to its eventual completion, loss of communication, or abandonment. The experience can be understood through several stages: - Users are introduced to the concept of the final signal and the end of a spacecraft's active mission. - Mission information is presented through an interactive interface rather than only through long blocks of text. - Users can explore individual mission stories and understand what happened during their final operational period. - Scientific information and mission facts are connected with visual storytelling. - Interactive elements help users understand concepts such as communication, distance, mission duration, spacecraft limitations, and the reasons why hardware can be left behind. - The project uses simulations or visual representations where appropriate to make difficult scientific concepts easier to understand. The website therefore combines information + visualization + interaction + storytelling to create an educational space-exploration experience. 3. What benefits does it have? The main benefit of the project is that it makes space science more accessible and engaging. Many NASA mission records contain large amounts of technical information that can be difficult for beginners to understand. After the Last Signal presents this information in a simpler and more visual format. The project provides several benefits: Educational benefit It helps students learn about spacecraft, space exploration, communication, mission endings, and scientific discoveries in an interactive manner. Increased public awareness It draws attention to spacecraft and equipment that are often forgotten after their missions end, showing that they can still have historical and scientific significance. Interactive learning Instead of simply reading information, users can explore the content and interact with different elements of the website. Better understanding of space missions The project helps users understand that spacecraft missions involve limitations such as power, communication distance, environmental conditions, and hardware durability. Storytelling The project gives a human and emotional perspective to scientific information. The "last signal" becomes a way of telling the story of a mission from its beginning to its final stage. Encouraging interest in STEM By combining technology, science, design, and storytelling, the project can encourage students to become more interested in astronomy, space science, engineering, and computer science. 4. What do you hope to achieve? Through After the Last Signal, our goal is to make NASA's space exploration history easier to discover, understand, and remember. We want users to realize that a spacecraft does not simply become irrelevant when its mission ends. The equipment left behind, the data collected, the discoveries made, and the engineering lessons learned can continue to contribute to humanity's understanding of space. We also hope to demonstrate how NASA's publicly available information can be transformed into an interactive educational experience. Our larger goals are to: - Make space science understandable to students and beginners. - Encourage curiosity about NASA missions and space exploration. - Preserve the stories of spacecraft whose missions have ended. - Help users understand the scientific and engineering challenges involved in space exploration. - Show how technology and storytelling can work together to communicate scientific information. - Inspire future students and developers to explore STEM fields. - Create an experience that makes users feel connected to the history of human exploration beyond Earth. Ultimately, we hope that users leave the project with one simple idea: A signal may stop, but the story and scientific legacy of a mission can continue. 5. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? The project was developed as a web-based digital experience using modern web-development technologies. Software and development tools - HTML — used to structure the webpages and content. - CSS — used for the visual design, layout, animations, colours, typography, and responsive presentation. - JavaScript — used to add interactivity and dynamic behaviour to the website. - GitHub / GitHub Pages — used for hosting and deploying the project as a publicly accessible website. - Web browser — used to test and interact with the final project. NASA resources and data NASA-related information and publicly available resources were used to build the educational content of the project. The NASA Space Apps Challenge encourages participants to use NASA's open data and resources to develop solutions and experiences around the challenge themes. Where applicable, NASA mission information, spacecraft records, imagery, and scientific resources are incorporated into the project's storytelling and educational sections. Hardware No specialized physical hardware is required for users to experience the project. It is designed to run through a standard web browser on devices such as: - Laptops - Desktop computers - Tablets - Smartphones This makes the project easily accessible to students and members of the public without requiring additional equipment. Overall Project Concept After the Last Signal transforms the ending of a spacecraft's mission into the beginning of a story. Rather than treating inactive or abandoned space hardware as simply "old equipment," the project presents these machines as part of humanity's history of exploration. Through interactive web design, scientific information, visualization, and storytelling, users can explore what happened before the final signal, why communication ended, and why the mission still matters. The project combines space science, NASA data, web development, education, and storytelling to create an accessible experience that encourages users to look beyond the final signal and discover the legacy that remains.
